chain.note: The cited study specifically reports ectopic MUC5B expression initiating ER stress in IPF lung.
UniProt supports the molecular function; its operation in IPF epithelium remains to be tested.

object.label: selective autophagic clearance of ubiquitinated cargo

falsification.description: In IPF-risk-genotype human bronchiolar organoids, normalize MUC5B while independently restoring TOLLIP; the hypothesis is falsified if neither intervention, alone or together, reduces ER-stress markers, ubiquitinated-protein burden, epithelial injury, or fibroblast-activating activity despite verified target engagement.
falsification.system: human bronchiolar organoid–fibroblast co-culture stratified by MUC5B/TOLLIP genotype

hypotheses.mechanism: Excess or ectopic MUC5B production in respiratory bronchioles imposes secretory/ER stress, while reduced TOLLIP activity would impair selective-autophagic disposal of ubiquitinated cargo and alter Toll-like receptor signaling. The combination is predicted to convert repeated airway injury into persistent epithelial stress and profibrotic remodeling rather than effective repair.
hypotheses.title: Ectopic MUC5B plus inadequate TOLLIP-dependent proteostasis sustains bronchiolar epithelial stress

chain.note: DSP supports both junctional organization and telomere maintenance; the relative contribution of each in IPF is unresolved.

object.label: desmosomal epithelial barrier and telomere protection

subject.label: telomere damage and epithelial repair failure

falsification.description: Introduce IPF-associated TERT and DSP perturbations singly and jointly into human alveolar epithelial progenitors, then serially passage them after injury; the hypothesis is falsified if restoring telomerase or DSP fails to rescue telomere-damage foci, clonogenic repair, epithelial barrier integrity, and profibrotic signaling despite confirmed molecular correction.
falsification.system: serially passaged human alveolar epithelial progenitors with DSP perturbation

hypotheses.mechanism: Reduced TERT function should limit telomere extension in renewing lung epithelial progenitors; impaired DSP can independently compromise desmosomal barrier organization and has a documented role in preventing telomere damage through TRF2. Their combined dysfunction is predicted to accelerate epithelial senescence or failed repair, enabling fibrotic remodeling after injury.
hypotheses.title: TERT and DSP converge on telomere protection and epithelial regenerative competence

chain.note: The retrieved evidence supports association, animal-model evidence, function, and cell specificity but does not resolve whether individual IPF variants act by loss of surfactant function or toxic misfolding.

object.label: alveolar type II cell injury and failed repair

subject.label: alveolar type II cell injury and failed repair

falsification.description: Correct the patient SFTPC allele in isogenic alveolar type II organoids and apply repeated mechanical or proteotoxic stress; the hypothesis is falsified if correction does not normalize surfactant processing, ER-stress/cell-death phenotypes, regenerative capacity, and fibroblast activation.

readout.label: alveolar type II cell stress and fibroblast activation

falsification.system: isogenic patient-derived alveolar type II organoids with fibroblast co-culture

hypotheses.mechanism: SFTPC is a BRICHOS-domain surfactant protein produced at very high levels by alveolar type II cells and is required for a stable low-tension alveolar surface film. Disease-associated loss, misprocessing, or toxic precursor accumulation is predicted to injure this regenerative cell compartment, producing recurrent alveolar collapse and maladaptive repair that culminates in fibrosis.
hypotheses.title: SFTPC dysfunction makes alveolar type II cells an initiating site of IPF

chain.note: The Rho-GAP domain and junctional/cytosolic localization motivate this step, but UniProt has no curated functional statement for FAM13A.

falsification.description: Edit the IPF-associated FAM13A haplotype into otherwise isogenic human lung epithelial cells and quantify Rho activity, junction dynamics, wound closure, and fibroblast activation; the hypothesis is falsified if the haplotype produces no reproducible change in any readout across airway and alveolar epithelial systems.

readout.label: Rho activity and epithelial wound repair

falsification.system: isogenic airway and alveolar epithelial monolayers with fibroblast co-culture

hypotheses.mechanism: FAM13A carries a Rho-GAP domain and localizes to cell-junction/cytosolic compartments in the available expression record, suggesting that IPF-associated variation may alter Rho-dependent epithelial shape, migration, or mechanotransduction during repair. Persistent misregulation is predicted to favor an abnormal wound state that activates fibroblasts, but the direction of effect and the relevant lung cell remain unresolved.
hypotheses.title: FAM13A alters junctional Rho signaling and epithelial wound repair
